issues: [CRITICAL] "ٱحْتَرَقَتْ — iḥtaraqat — Form VIII of حرق. Reflexive. The garden didn't just burn. It BURNED FROM WITHIN ITSELF... The destruction is INTERNAL." (and in the hidden Step-0 block: "it burned from WITHIN itself. Not set on fire by an external source") — Form VIII اِحْتَرَقَ here is the muṭāwiʿ (resultative) of أَحْرَقَ, i.e. 'it was consumed by fire', not self-combustion. The ayah itself names the external agent: فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌ فِيهِ نَارٌ فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ. The paired al-Muyassar on 2:266 states it flatly: هبَّت عليه ريح شديدة، فيها نار محرقة فأحرقته — a wind carrying consuming fire burned it. The file's reading contradicts both the Quranic wording and its own tafsir, and the whole 'the destruction is internal' theological beat rests on it.

[MINOR] "إِعْصَارٌ — i'ṣār — is a Form IV maṣdar from عصر — to squeeze, to press. A whirlwind that CAUSES squeezing" — إعصار is a jāmid noun that happens to sit on the إفْعَال pattern; it is not the maṣdar of a Form IV verb أعصر in use here, and no source in the report derives 'causes squeezing' from it. The lexical link to عصر is defensible; the morphological label and the causative gloss are over-read.
summary: Exceptionally well-sourced file — every attribution I could check against the correctly-paired report is exact: al-Ṭabarī's مردودة إلى 2:245 link, his قولٌ جميل ودعاءُ الرجل لأخيه المسلم and سترٌ منه عليه لما علم من خَلَّته gloss on 2:263, al-Muyassar's زُرِعتْ في أرض طيبة, بحسب ما يقوم بقلب المنفق من الإيمان والإخلاص, عفو عما بدر مِن السائل مِن إلحافٍ في السؤال and هكذا حال غير المخلصين في نفقاتهم, Ibn Kathīr's ten-to-seven-hundred range, his īmānan wa-ḥtisāban parallel on تثبيتا, and the Bukhārī ʿUmar/Ibn ʿAbbās scene at 2:266. Saʿīd b. Jubayr and Makḥūl are quoted correctly from Ibn Kathīr at 2:261. Form IDs for أنبتت (IV), تبطلوا (IV), رئاء (III maṣdar), ابتغاء (VIII), تثبيتا (II) and تتفكرون (V) are all correct. The single real defect is the iḥtaraqat 'burned from within' claim, which contradicts the ayah and al-Muyassar. Report note: the paired report exhibits the measured duplication defect — the identical Ibn Kathīr block ('To Remind About Charity Given is Forbidden') is repeated verbatim under 2:262, 2:263 and 2:264, and most Ibn Kathīr/al-Ṭabarī blocks are truncated mid-sentence. The tadabbur did not inherit that error; it only draws Ibn Kathīr from the non-duplicated 2:261, 2:265 and 2:266 blocks.

issues: [MODERATE] "the Prophet ﷺ is described in Surah At-Tawbah (9:128) as رَحِيمٌ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ — 'merciful toward the believers.'" — the Arabic is presented as the wording of 9:128 but is not it. Canonical text: بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ (confirmed via canonical-verse.mjs, and matching the al-Ṭabarī block in the paired report). The words have been reordered and رءوف dropped. Not fabricated and the argument it supports (رحيم is predicable of a human, رحمن is not) survives intact — hence MODERATE rather than CRITICAL — but a reordered string should not be presented as the ayah's wording.

[MINOR] "The Basran school... said the implied verb comes *before* the phrase: أَبْدَأُ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ... The Kufan school said no — the structure is: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ابْتِدَائِي" — the two schools are attached to the right taqdīrs, but the classical dispute is verb-estimation (Basran) vs. noun-estimation (Kufan), not word order. The file recasts it as a before/after positioning question and then draws a theological contrast ('the human reaching for divine help' vs. 'the human placing himself on a divine foundation') from that recast axis. Both conclusions are defensible; the framing of the disagreement is not what the grammarians were arguing about.

[MINOR] "The word اسم — 'name' — normally begins with a hamzah: إِسْم... It's called همزة الوصل" — the word is written with hamzat qaṭʿ (إِسْم) in the same sentence that correctly identifies it as hamzat waṣl; it should be ٱسْم / اِسْم.
summary: The old CRITICAL does not survive correct pairing. Every substantive linguistic claim holds: فَعْلَان as the overflow/imtilāʾ pattern (ghaḍbān, ʿaṭshān, jawʿān) and فَعِيل as the pattern of settled attribute are standard ṣarf; the root of اسم traced to سمو on the Basran view is the majority position and matches the morphology tags; the deleted-verb argument is exactly what al-Ṭabarī says in the paired report (الباء ... مقتضية فعلا يكون لها جالبا, ولا فعل معها ظاهر). The al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr readings of الرحمن/الرحيم as breadth-vs-specificity and universal-vs-believers align with al-Muyassar in the report (ذي الرحمة العامة ... الرحيم بالمؤمنين); al-Qurṭubī's exclusivity point (الرحمن is not predicable of creation) is correctly his. Residual defects are the 9:128 misquotation and two presentational slips.

issues: [MODERATE] "this comes directly from ayah 56 of this same surah's surrounding context, where Allah says, huwa-lladhī yuṣallī ʿalaykum wa malā'ikatuhu" — the quoted verse is 33:43 (هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَلِّى عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلَـٰٓئِكَتُهُۥ, confirmed via canonical-verse.mjs), not ayah 56, which is the verse under study. The frontmatter's related_ayahs correctly lists 33:43, so this is a citation slip in the body, but it names the wrong ayah as the source of a quotation and then contradicts itself two lines later ('Earlier in this very surah').

[MODERATE] "The root ص ل و carries a base meaning that the lexicographers describe as connection, attention, facing toward... The classical lexicons — Lisān al-ʿArab, Mufradāt al-Rāghib, Tāj al-ʿArūs — circle around this same idea." — three lexicons are named for a lexical base they do not give. Lisān and Tāj give الدُّعاء والاستغفار as the base of الصلاة (plus the الصَّلَوان / hip-bone derivation); al-Rāghib likewise routes it through duʿāʾ and الصَّلا. 'Turning toward / connection' is the file's own synthesis presented as documented lexicography. Note this is separable from the file's downstream claims, which ARE well sourced: Allah's ṣalāh as praise-before-the-angels/mercy and the angels' as duʿāʾ match Ibn Kathīr (Abu al-ʿĀliyah: 'Allah's Salah is His praising him before the angels, and the Salah of the angels is their supplication') and al-Ṭabarī (يبرّكون / أن الله يرحم النبي، وتدعو...) in the paired report.

[MODERATE] "There is no other action in the Quran where this happens quite like this. There is no other ayah where Allah describes Himself doing an action and then turns to you in the same sentence and says: and you do it too." — an absolute uniqueness claim with no support in any source in the report, and there are counterexamples (2:152 فَٱذْكُرُونِى أَذْكُرْكُمْ; and 33:43 in this same surah, which the file itself quotes). Stated as fact, not as rhetorical emphasis.
[MINOR] Closing du'a: "Allāhumma, You who *yuṣallūna* upon Your Prophet" — يصلّون is 3rd-person plural; addressing Allah in the vocative with it is ungrammatical. تُصلّي would be required.
summary: The old CRITICAL is an artifact. The core reading is sound and matches the paired report: muḍāriʿ يُصَلُّونَ vs. imperative صَلُّوا is correctly identified; تَسْلِيمًا as mafʿūl muṭlaq intensifying سَلِّمُوا is standard and correct; the three-actor / three-realities treatment reproduces the Bukhārī–Abū al-ʿĀliyah distinction that Ibn Kathīr carries in the report, and al-Jalalayn's اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلى سَيِّدنا مُحَمَّد وسَلِّمْ supports the practical framing. The ṣalāh-without-intensifier asymmetry is presented honestly as a composite of scholarly angles ('One angle... Another angle... A third angle'). The defects are a wrong ayah number on a real quotation, a lexical base attributed to three named lexicons that do not give it, and an unsupported Quran-wide uniqueness claim. Note frontmatter still carries validated: false.

issues: [CRITICAL] "كُلٌّ (kullun) with the tanwīn... is grammatically marked as indefinite and exhaustive at the same time... Allah did not say kulluhum lahū qānitūn — 'all of them are obedient to Him,' which would fence the group to those just mentioned... The tanwīn pries the fence open." — this is backwards, and the construction described does not exist. The tanwīn on كُلٌّ here is تنوين العِوَض, compensating for the elided muḍāf ilayh: كُلٌّ is precisely equivalent to كُلُّهُمْ and refers back to the group just named (the standard iʿrāb for both 30:26 and 2:116). The file invents a 'universal and unbounded' function for the tanwīn, contrasts it against the very form it is a substitute for, and then makes that invented grammar the load-bearing proof of its central 'there is no exception' thesis. The illustrative contrast (كُلُّ الرِّجَال vs. كُلٌّ) does not describe Arabic usage.

[MODERATE] "Notice the absence. Where is the exception?... No 'except those who turned away'... from that reality, there is no exception... He is qānit. Whether he knows it or not." — stated with flat certainty where the paired al-Ṭabarī raises exactly this as an open question and records ikhtilāf: فيقول قائل: وكيف قيل ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ﴾ وقد علم أن أكثر الإنس والجنّ له عاصون؟ فنقول: اختلف أهل التأويل في تأويل ذلك. The file's four 'camera angles' (Ibn ʿAbbās muqirrūn, Mujāhid muṭīʿūn, awe, silence) are all internal to the everyone-is-included frame; the recorded disagreement about the scope itself is never surfaced.

[MINOR] Element One argues مَن restricts the ayah to conscious beings — "The ayah is no longer telling you 'Allah owns the rocks'" — and the rest of the file then makes stones, stars, liver cells, blood cells, atoms and air pressure the subjects of qunūt. Internally inconsistent. (The broad reading is in fact supported by al-Muyassar in the report — من الملائكة والإنس والجن والحيوان والنبات والجماد — but that source is never cited, and it cuts against the file's own مَن/مَا argument.)
[MINOR] "Al-Rāzī sits with it in his commentary" — al-Rāzī is not among the four sources in the paired report and the claim is unverifiable from it; plausible but unsupported.

[MINOR] passage_context: "a sustained sequence of 'min āyātihi'... that runs through the middle of Surah Ar-Rūm (verses 20-27)" — the وَمِنْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ markers run 20–25; 26 and 27 do not carry the formula.
summary: The old CRITICAL survives correct pairing, though not for the reason the mispaired review would have given. Much of the file is solid: قَانِتُونَ as ism al-fāʿil rather than verb is correct; the مَن/مَا contrast with 2:116 uses the real text of both verses (verified) and matches al-Ṭabarī's من ملك وجنّ وإنس; the takhṣīṣ-by-fronting reading of لَّهُۥ قَـٰنِتُونَ is standard balāghah; قُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَـٰنِتِينَ (2:238) is quoted accurately; the four glosses render 'obedient/acknowledging' as al-Ṭabarī, al-Jalalayn (مُطِيعُونَ) and al-Muyassar all do. The disqualifying problem is the fabricated function assigned to the tanwīn on كُلّ — it is تنوين العوض, an exact stand-in for كُلُّهُمْ, and the file argues the opposite in order to ground its no-exception thesis. Compounded by presenting a question al-Ṭabarī explicitly flags as contested as though it were settled.

issues: [MODERATE] "Kullun (each/every) is the grammatical subject — so the most natural reading is that each creature knows its own salah" — the paired report leans the other way. Al-Jalalayn glosses it by inserting the subject outright: ﴿كُلّ قَدْ عَلِمَ﴾ اللَّه ﴿صَلاته وتَسْبِيحه﴾, and the Ibn Kathīr rendering in the report reads 'Of each one He knows indeed his Salah and his glorification.' Al-Muyassar supports the creature side only obliquely (كل مخلوق قد أرشده الله كيف يصلي له). The file does name the second reading and says 'both are true,' which is honest — but calling the creature-knows reading 'the most natural' understates the report, and the entire Theme Two ('the bird already knew', 'we are the only creature who has to be taught') plus the one-sentence distillation rest on the side the report's sources treat as secondary.

[MINOR] The file's own translation renders مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ as "whatever is in the heavens and the earth" and then applies the ayah to mountains, fish, dust and atoms. That application is legitimate — but it needs the taghlīb point al-Jalalayn supplies in the report (فِيهِ تَغْلِيب العاقِل), which is never mentioned; and it sits oddly beside the strict مَن = rational-beings-only argument this corpus makes elsewhere on 30:26.
[MINOR] "the most luminous parabola in the Quran" — 'parabola' for 'parable'.
summary: The old CRITICAL is an artifact. The linguistics check out: يُسَبِّحُ is correctly Form II of س-ب-ح, the physical base 'to swim / move far out through a medium' is what the lexicons give, and the imperfect-as-continuous reading is right. صَـٰٓفَّـٰتٍ as an accusative ḥāl is confirmed verbatim by al-Jalalayn in the paired report (﴿صافّات﴾ حال باسِطات أجْنِحَتهنَّ), and the wings-outspread + ranks-in-formation double sense is standard. قَدْ + māḍī as settled completion is correct. The 17:44 quotation is exact (verified), as is the 37:1 allusion. The ikhtilāf on who does the knowing is disclosed rather than hidden — the only real charge is that the file picks the lighter-supported side as 'most natural' and hangs its whole second half on it. Frontmatter still carries validated: false.
